evidence_quote: Cloning and sequencing of complementary DNA encoding for CD18 in this patient revealed two mutant alleles, each representing a point mutation in the coding region of CD18 and resulting in an amino acid substitution.
note: One patient with partial CD18 deficiency; patient data are mainly laboratory (CD18 expression) with recurrent bacterial infections.

evidence_quote: Flow cytometric analysis of the surface expression of adhesion receptors on isolated cells (Fig. 1) confirmed a complete absence of CD18 on neutrophils from the LAD-I patient (17) and normal expression on control cells and LAD-II neutrophils (19).
note: Close call: mainly a neutrophil function study, but it reports individual data (absent CD18) for one LAD-I patient; the second patient has LAD-II.

evidence_quote: A structural defect (deletion or point mutation) in the 𝛃2 subunit (with special attention to the transmembrane and cytoplasmic tail) was excluded by sequencing CD18 cDNA, indicating that this patient did not suffer from classical LAD-1.
note: LAD-1/variant with normal CD11/CD18 expression and no CD18 defect on sequencing; not classical LAD-I.

evidence_quote: Sequencing of the patient's two CD18 alleles revealed the mutations S138P and G273R.
note: Expressed but nonfunctional beta2 integrins (40-60% expression); paper presents the two CD18 mutations as causing an LAD-1-like phenotype.

evidence_quote: We report on a child with LAD-1, dysmorphic features, and growth retardation caused by a combination of a point mutation in ITGB2 and a gross deletion resulting in r(21).
note: ITGB2 nonsense variant on one allele and a 21q22.3-qter deletion (ring 21) removing ITGB2 on the other.

evidence_quote: A total of five consecutive patients with LAD-I (two boys and three girls) underwent UCBT at our medical center from September 2016 to September 2018.
note: Text says ITGB2 mutations were found in all five but names no variant; per-patient Tables 2-4 (Table 4: 9 earlier UCBT patients) are links only, not in the text.

evidence_quote: Invitae primary immunodeficiency panel reported a homozygous variant in ITGB2 gene c.295del (p.Ser99Profs*5).
note: Six patients in a per-patient table; variants reported for two.
